patterns.title: Replaceable Wear Units
patterns.topical_cross_listing: Assembly, Maintenance, and Renewal; not a second parent or definition.
patterns.summary: Put predictable wear in separately renewable parts so useful supporting equipment can remain after renewal.

identity_resolution.boundary: This entry places a predictable wear location in a separately renewable element. Segmentation chooses manageable units generally; Standardized Module Interfaces preserves substitution contracts; Architecture Repairable Connections addresses access and connections in buildings; Business Repair and Maintenance concerns an offering and revenue.

use_when: Recurring wear is concentrated in a contact surface or limited region.
Renewing the worn region would otherwise involve replacing a useful supporting structure or shaft.
A complete access, retention, and replacement route can be designed for a liner, sleeve, shoe, or bushing.
goals: Expose the full service task and interfaces
mechanisms: Separate renewable contact element from retained support
Suitable wear surface and usable allowance
Stable support and retention through the permitted condition
not_ideal_when: Damage bypasses the insert into the retained component.
The underlying structure or shaft is no longer suitable.
The new interfaces, obstruction, or service work outweigh the achievable benefit.
example_user_queries: Our chute wears through in one spot but most of the structure is still sound.
Can we replace the rubbing surface instead of the whole shaft?
The wear insert is bolted in but there is no way to take it out.
How should we choose the boundary of a renewable wear part?
We keep rebuilding the chute floor after local abrasion.
Should we use a coating or a separately replaceable liner?
The average liner thickness looks fine but one small region is worn out.
How do we protect a pump shaft from packing-contact damage?
Our replaceable liner needs major dismantling before it can be reached.
Does adding a wear sleeve guarantee shorter maintenance downtime?
The new liner wears rapidly again after every replacement.
What must remain intact when a wear unit is renewed?

related_patterns.title: Segmentation
related_patterns.relationship: Direct parent. This child defines a unit around predictable wear rather than another handling or change requirement.

related_patterns.title: Functional Surfaces
related_patterns.relationship: Can complement a wear unit through treatment or coating; does not necessarily create a separately replaceable element.

related_patterns.title: Reversible Joining
related_patterns.relationship: Supports release and restoration but does not choose a wear location or guarantee a complete removal route.

related_patterns.title: Condition-Based Maintenance
related_patterns.relationship: Chooses service timing from evidence; a renewable wear unit can also use another suitable maintenance plan.

complementary_authored_pattern.relationship: Preserves required replacement fit and boundary behavior.

worked_examples.name: Six-panel conveyor transfer chute
worked_examples.baseline: Material contacts the structural floor directly, so local wear involves structural work.
worked_examples.intervention: Six individually retained liners place the contact wear in renewable panels while retaining a suitable shell.
worked_examples.limits: The readings and 6 mm criterion are invented. They are not a recommended thickness, measured installation, load rating, wear rate, or remaining-life prediction. Retained shell and attachments still require assessment.

worked_examples.name: Packed-gland pump shaft sleeve
worked_examples.intervention: A rotating sleeve provides the contact surface for stationary packing, allowing renewal while retaining a suitable shaft.
worked_examples.limits: Not a universal mechanical-seal arrangement, numerical wear limit, or executable dismantling procedure. No service-time or leakage improvement is claimed.

worked_examples.name: Wear insert trapped behind access opening
held_fixed: straight withdrawal enforced by retained guides
worked_examples.limits: One-dimensional geometry only. Rotation is explicitly unavailable. Does not establish adequate handling or tool space, or the structural and sealing acceptability of a changed opening. Major dismantling can defeat local service while material-retention benefits may still remain.

source_notes.source: Metso, Wear lining impact plates for transfer chutes
source_notes.basis: Read discussion of transfer-chute impact and sliding abrasion and bolted Rockbox liner arrangements.
source_notes.boundary: No advertised wear-life gain is transferred to the original fictional flat-panel design; no manufacturer geometry is traced.

source_notes.basis: Read protection against seal-related mechanical damage and responsibilities for retention, axial allowance, and leakage paths.
source_notes.boundary: No fit, sleeve material, life, or capacity is selected from the source.

source_notes.basis: Read explanation of stationary packing acting on shaft-protecting sleeves and the role of friction/cooling conditions.
source_notes.boundary: The example is specifically a packed gland. Product operating limits and numerical leakage rates are not reused.

source_notes.source: PumpWorks PWA-IL installation/operation/maintenance manual, MAINT-10 (PDF page 41)
source_notes.basis: Read Inspection and Replacement: sleeve surface in the stuffing-box area must be smooth and free from grooves; replacement criterion is stated for that equipment.
source_notes.boundary: Not a universal wear threshold or instruction to replace every shaft-seal sleeve. The full dismantling procedure is not reproduced.

source_notes.source: Martin Engineering, External Wear Liner Retrofit Kit, L3803-03/19
source_notes.basis: Read mounting outside the existing skirtboard without interfering with supports and the stated external service access.
source_notes.boundary: A product-specific example of deliberate access, not a claim that all liners can be serviced externally or without shutdown.

research_lead_status.lead: University of Michigan Design Heuristics handout
research_lead_status.status: Not used as evidence. The direct PDF fetch returned HTTP 403 during earlier research in this chat; this taxonomy is not presented as its official card set.

research_lead_status.lead: J. E. Gordon, Structures: Or Why Things Don't Fall Down
research_lead_status.status: Contextual reading lead only. No specific book passage, illustration, numerical wear criterion, or service-life claim is attributed without reading it.
Direct open was inaccessible through the web tool; accessible primary KSB and PumpWorks sources supplied the sleeve mechanism and model-specific inspection evidence instead.

graphics.decision: Three static explanatory SVG figures and phone companions; no widget.
graphics.reason: The renewal boundary, shaft/sleeve contact, and blocked/clear removal route are inspectable in fixed drawings. The supplied thickness readings are a decision fixture rather than a wear simulation.
graphics.style: Approved fixed-white editorial engineering drawings with regular Helvetica Neue, fine neutral lines, and restrained green.
graphics.provenance: Original schematic geometry and labels. No manufacturer drawings or book figures traced, no external photographs, no generated raster illustrations.
